newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt plans to hold Israel summit for now-Moussa.
newsitem.headline: Egypt plans to hold Israel summit for now-Moussa.

text.p: Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said on Sunday his country was not considering scrapping a planned Egyptian-Israeli summit meeting for now and was waiting for the results of an envoy's visit to Israel.

"We're not talking about this possibility (cancelling the meeting) right now and we're waiting for the results of the contacts that (Egyptian political adviser) Osama el-Baz is currently making," Moussa told reporters.

He was responding to a question about whether Egypt would still host a meeting on Tuesday in a Red Sea resort between Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and President Hosni Mubarak if Baz failed to "get any Israeli compromises".
Baz was in Tel Aviv on Sunday for his second round of meetings in Israel in 48 hours to pave the way for the summit.
His visit is part of efforts to resume Palestinian-Israeli talks stalled since March by Israel's construction of a Jewish settlement in East Jerusalem on land claimed by both sides.

The Palestinians say they will resume talks only when Israel halts work on the settlement -- a view that peace mediator Egypt supports -- but Israel has said it will continue building at the hillside called Jabal Abu Ghneim or Har Homa.

Mubarak has previously suggested halting settlement activity for six months but on Saturday he told a news conference after meeting Jordan's King Hussein that he was sending Baz to Israel without any preconditions.
On Sunday, Israel's Yedioth Ahronoth daily said the summit was in danger of being cancelled because of Israel's refusal to to stop building the settlement. A Netanyahu aide denied this.
